title: Entanglement entropy in holographic CFTs with generic boundaries
abstract: Entanglement entropy in holographic conformal field theories with boundaries of generic spacetime signature cannot be described entirely within the standard holographic duality to a real bulk spacetime. We show, both in static and time-dependent setups, that an exact match with the conformal field theory predictions in two boundary dimensions entails an extension of the dual spacetime to complex coordinates. As a consequence, relevant bulk objects such as Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces and branes are in general complex, yet anchored on a real asymptotic boundary preserving the physical meaning of field-theoretical quantities. We also provide a third numerical check of the holographic prediction with a two-dimensional system of free Gaussian fermions exhibiting the same asymptotic regimes across different entanglement phases.
summary: This work extends the holographic description of entanglement entropy to CFTs with boundaries of generic spacetime signature. It demonstrates that achieving consistency requires complexifying the dual bulk spacetime, forcing relevant geometric objects like extremal surfaces to possess complex coordinates. This complexification successfully reproduces known results from boundary quantum field theory calculations.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of calculating entanglement entropy in holographic Conformal Field Theories (CFTs) when the boundary conditions are generic, particularly those leading to spacelike boundaries.
main_result: To maintain consistency with CFT predictions for generic boundaries, the dual bulk spacetime geometry, including the Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces and branes, must be extended into complex coordinates.
method: The authors employ the holographic duality (AdS/CFT) framework, calculating entanglement entropy via the area of extremal surfaces (RT formula) and comparing this result to predictions derived from the boundary CFT (e.g., twist operator correlators).
model_or_system: The model involves holographic CFTs dual to gravitational theories, specifically analyzing entanglement entropy in static and time-dependent setups with boundaries of generic spacetime signature, including free Gaussian fermions as a numerical check.
key_observables: Entanglement Entropy ($S_A$), which is calculated as $\min(	ext{Re } S_{	ext{con}}, 	ext{Re } S_{	ext{dis}})$, and the complex geodesic length ($D_{	ext{disc}}$).
important_parameters: The ratio of region size ($L$) to the brane location ($t_0$), and the boundary cutoff $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The standard real Lorentzian AdS/BCFT prescription fails for general causal structures; the selection of the dominant saddle point requires minimizing the *real part* of the area.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the difference between real (timelike) and complex (spacelike) anchoring points for RT surfaces, and plot the regularized entropy showing a phase transition matching Gaussian free fermion results.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by first noting the failure of real bulk descriptions for spacelike boundaries, then deriving the necessary complex extensions for the RT surfaces and branes, and finally confirming the results by matching the complex geodesic length to known boundary CFT calculations.
why_interesting: The necessity of complexifying the bulk geometry to match boundary quantum field theory results provides a powerful, non-trivial constraint on the holographic duality, suggesting that the mathematical structure of the dual spacetime must be generalized beyond simple Lorentzian signatures.
